name: craftsman
description: Cross-project engineering craft — a whole-project audit orchestrator plus ten active, opinionated domain skills plus the craft-fix companion. craft-audit (the front door) assesses a whole project for production-readiness: it discovers the project's shape, decides which domains apply, and plans/tracks the audit in a .craftsman/ workspace — with derived per-domain readiness grades and re-run intelligence (staleness detection plus finding-by-finding diffing across runs) — routing findings to the domain skills, which each expose an audit checklist the orchestrator turns into the plan. craft-fix then drives the fixes: it re-verifies each pick against current code, batches by surface, and never marks a finding fixed itself — only a re-run's re-observation of the finding can, per "not seen ≠ fixed". Built for taking a vibe-coded MVP to enterprise-grade. The ten domains, each with a complete reference set: craft-ux (design-system layer model, motion, accessibility, two-pass review + token scanner), craft-frontend (architecture, state, data-fetching, forms, performance), craft-backend (API design, auth, validation, error contract, side-effects), craft-db (schema, migrations, access patterns, indexing, integrity), craft-security (authz, input/output, secrets, headers/CORS, supply-chain), craft-infra (config, build/release, CI/CD, runtime health, scale/resilience), craft-observability (Sentry, logging, Grafana, SLOs/alerts, serverless), craft-testing (strategy, test design, killing flaky tests, frontend & backend/data testing), craft-lint (ESLint resolved-rule extraction, typed linting, zero-warning CI gates, and lint config hardening), and craft-ai (LLM integrations — prompt injection, key/spend safety, PII-to-model APIs, reliability/evals). Each skill triggers once per domain, pushes depth into references/, and discovers project specifics from the repo rather than hardcoding them. A worked example of a finished audit ships under examples/; drafts/ incubates future domains until their references are filled.
